title: Stop the log scanner from running out of file handles

blocks.text: The support team's service runs `LogScanner.countErrors(dir)` every few minutes to show how many `ERROR` lines today's logs hold. The numbers are right, and the service runs fine for a day or two. Then every scan, and everything else in the process that opens a file, fails with `Too many open files`, until someone restarts it.

items: `listLogs(dir)`: the `.log` files of the directory, sorted by name;
`errorsIn(log)`: how many lines of one log contain `ERROR`.

blocks.text: Open the directory with `openDir` and each log with `openLog`, never with `Files` directly: the tests replace those two methods to watch what the scanner opens. A log can fail while it is being read (a disk unmounted, a file truncated under you); that failure should reach the caller of `countErrors`. About seven lines in total.
When you're done, the scanner can run every few minutes for weeks and hold no file open between scans, whether a scan succeeds or fails.

cases.says: the scanner counts the lines containing ERROR across every .log file of the directory
only files ending in .log are scanned, in name order
every log stream the scanner opens is closed once its errors are counted
the stream that lists the directory is closed too, not only the streams over the logs
a log whose reading fails partway is still closed before the failure reaches the caller

origin.section: A Stream Over a File Holds It Open Until close(), Not Until the Terminal Operation

concepts: A stream from Files.lines, Files.list or Files.walk keeps its file or directory open after the terminal operation, until close(); try-with-resources closes it even when reading fails.
